verdict.rationale: Exa documents ready-made agent tool consumption. It offers a hosted MCP server that works in any MCP client, an exa-js `web_search` tool helper for OpenAI or Anthropic tool loops, an official OpenAI plugin, and agent skills, so the core of plugging it into an agent as a tool is clearly delivered. The evidence does not show explicit published function-calling JSON schemas, and no third-party agent-framework integrations (e.g. framework adapters) are named. missing for 10: explicitly documented function-calling tool schemas, named agent-framework integrations beyond OpenAI/Anthropic loops and MCP, independent hands-on corroboration of the tool-call integrations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug the API into an agent as a ready-made tool, with function-calling schemas and agent-framework integrations designed for direct tool-call consumption

citations.quote: Use Exa as a `web_search` tool in an OpenAI or Anthropic loop. Call `webSearch()` with no arguments to get Exa's recommended settings for agentic search
Tool-using agents can call Exa without writing code through the hosted MCP server at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp
Connect ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Grok, Cursor, and any other MCP client to Exa's web search, page fetching, Exa Agent, and Exa Connect tools.
Exa is an official plugin in OpenAI's plugin directory, which includes the hosted MCP server plus Exa's `search` and `exa-agent` skills.
the `agent_run` tool is enabled by default, so you can run multi-step research, list-building, enrichment, and structured output from Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients.
